units.scenario: Nam meets Yamada-sensei again after a long break and asks how he is, then uses the greetings for leaving home, going to bed and leaving work before others.
Nam reads simple hiragana words — seafood and snacks on a menu, things around him — aloud to Yuki, who checks his reading.
At a small welcome party Nam introduces himself — name, country, languages — then introduces Yuki to another guest and asks what the guests do.
Walking around town with Yuki, Nam reads Japanese dish names on a menu and words on signs.
At a fruit stall Nam buys several pieces of fruit, then tells a new classmate his age, his student number and his year at university.
Nam and Yuki have lunch at a small restaurant: they choose drinks, hot or cold, talk about fruit and tastes, and use table manners.
Nam and Yuki look at fruit, flags and a traffic light and ask each other what colour things are and which colours they like.
Nam and Yuki talk about pets, farm animals and wild animals: which ones they like, which are cute or strong, and which live in Japan or Thailand.
Yuki asks Nam about the weather in Bangkok; they compare hot Thai days and sudden storms with Japanese winter, and talk about flowers of each season.
Nam and Yuki talk about people they know — classmates, Yamada-sensei and a famous manga artist — and what they are like.
Nam and Yuki find out what each other likes and dislikes — music, films, sports and food — and why.
Yuki tells Nam about her busy, surprising day; Nam reacts naturally (ほんとうですか, なるほど), says how he feels and answers her compliment on his Japanese modestly.
Nam and Yuki plan a day out of the city — the sea or the mountains — and talk about what they can see there and what they like to do outdoors.
In Yamada-sensei's Japanese class Nam does not understand a word, asks him to repeat it slowly and asks how to say a Thai word in Japanese.
Yuki tells Nam about Japanese culture — public baths, castles and torii gates, summer festivals, sumo and ninja — and asks what Nam likes or finds interesting.
Nam visits Yuki's family in Japan at New Year: he greets them at the door, wishes them a happy New Year, receives a small gift, and later wishes Yuki good luck.
Nam reads a hiragana postcard and Japanese city names aloud with Yuki, paying attention to っ, small ゃゅょ and long vowels.
Nam reads country names and a festival poster in katakana and shows Yuki how Thai places and dishes are written in katakana.
Yuki and Nam compare their timetables for the week, talk about yesterday and the day after tomorrow, and fix a date to meet.
Nam shops for a bag: he points at bags near and far, asks about other colours and prices, and pays by card or cash.
Nam asks a passer-by the way to a park and a library and how to get there by train: which platform, where to change and where to get off.
Yuki asks Nam about his daily routine and his family in Bangkok — his parents and his younger sister Fah — and Nam asks about Yuki's brother.
Before a winter trip to Hokkaido, Nam shops for a warm jacket: he asks for another colour and a bigger size, tries it on and decides.
Yuki visits Nam's family home in Bangkok; Nam shows her the rooms and says where things and the family's pet are.
At a convenience store Nam buys lunch and drinks: the clerk asks whether to heat the bento and whether he needs chopsticks or a spoon, and Nam pays.
Nam and Yuki eat out: they say how many they are, order coffee and a lunch set, ask for a fork and napkins, and pay together.
Nam phones Yuki's family in Japan: he says hello, asks for Yuki, leaves his number, and they agree on a time for a video call with the time difference in mind.
Nam feels unwell before class; he tells Yuki where it hurts, and they go to a pharmacy for cold medicine, a mask and plasters.
Yuki asks Nam about his plans for the summer holidays; they look at a calendar, talk about Japanese holidays like Golden Week and Obon, and Nam says where he wants to go.
Nam and Yuki talk about what they do in their free time and what they did last weekend.
Nam travels to Kyoto: at the hotel he asks for a single room for two nights and an extra blanket, visits a museum, buys souvenirs, and later tells Yuki about the trip.
On his trip in Japan Nam loses his wallet on the train; he asks a station attendant for help and reports it at the police box (こうばん).

B is Yuki, who is recruiting members for her university club at the club fair. Nam must talk about their hobbies, say what they did last weekend and what they can do, such as cooking Thai food or playing an instrument, and decide whether to join.
B is a doctor at a clinic near the university. Nam must say where it hurts and since when, describe the symptoms, and check how and when to take the medicine.
B is Yamada-sensei in an advising session. Nam must talk about their major, compare their favourite and most difficult subjects, and say what job they want after graduating.
B is Yuki on the phone. Nam must invite Yuki to an event, agree on the day, time and meeting place, and politely turn down one of Yuki's suggestions.
B is the manager of Nam's student dormitory on moving-in day. Nam must ask for help and information, ask permission (cooking late, having a guest) and check which dormitory rules must be followed.
B is Yuki at a café after the holidays. Nam must describe a trip (what it was like and what they did) and ask and answer questions about experiences, such as whether Yuki has ever been to Thailand.
B is Yuki chatting with Nam over lunch. Nam must switch to plain (casual) forms to talk about plans and yesterday, ask questions with 〜の？ and explain things with 〜んだ.
B is Yuki planning a weekend outing with Nam. Nam must check the weather forecast with her, say what the weather may be like and suggest a plan for both rain and sunshine.

B is Yuki, who is waiting with Nam for a friend at a busy station and then helps Nam pick an outfit for a party. Nam must describe what people are wearing and what they look like, and say what is too flashy, too plain or too tight.
B is Yuki, who wants to learn to cook a Thai dish. Nam must name the ingredients, explain the steps in order and give tips (what to get ready first, what not to add, how to tell when it is done).
B is the manager of a convenience store interviewing Nam for a part-time job. Nam must answer questions about experience and free days, and ask about pay, shifts and the rules.
B is a clerk at a post office counter. Nam must send a parcel to Thailand, choose how to send it, fill in the form and ask about the price and how long delivery takes.

B is Yuki, who wants to start exercising. Nam must talk about the sports they play or watch, compare them, describe a match result and give advice on how to start (what is better to do and not to do).
B is Yuki, who is curious about Thai festivals. Nam must explain a Thai festival (when it is held and what people do), ask about a Japanese summer festival and agree to go together.
B is Yuki helping Nam choose a present. Nam must talk about presents they have given and received, ask Yuki's advice on what to give Yamada-sensei, and thank someone properly for a gift.
B is a clerk at a mobile phone shop. Nam must say what they need from a new phone and plan, ask how to set it up, and compare which plan is easier to use and cheaper.

B is Yamada-sensei leading a class discussion about student life. Nam must give and explain an opinion on topics such as part-time jobs for students and pass on a message from Yuki, who is absent today.
B is Yuki planning a spring-break trip with Nam. Nam must suggest where to go, say what they intend to do there, and agree on transport, budget and schedule.
B is the receptionist at a ryokan. Nam must check in, ask about meals, the baths and check-out time, and ask what to do about a problem in the room.
B is a station attendant at a ticket office. Nam has missed a connection because of a delay and must ask about refunds, the next express or local train and seat options, and decide what to do.
B is Yamada-sensei in a progress interview before the JLPT. Nam must say what they can and cannot do in Japanese now, describe how their skills have changed, and ask for advice on how to study.
B is Yuki, whose laptop has broken just before a deadline. Nam must offer help, tell her what friends have done for them before, and politely ask Yuki for a favour in return.
B is Yuki, who looks tired and worried before a job interview. Nam must notice how she seems, ask what is wrong, share how they feel themselves and cheer her up.

B is Yuki chatting about what is going on around campus. Nam must pass on news they heard and say where they heard it, guess what is happening from what they can see, and react naturally to Yuki's news.
B is an estate agent. Nam must describe the room they want (rent, distance from the station, sunlight), ask about conditions such as the deposit and contract, and arrange a viewing.

B is a neighbour who comes to complain politely that Nam put rubbish out on the wrong day. Nam must apologise, ask about the rules (which day, which bag) and politely raise a problem of their own (noise from upstairs).
B is a waiter at a busy izakaya. Nam is ordering for a group and must ask for recommendations, order the right quantities, ask for a dish to be made less spicy, and sort out the bill.
B is a customer-service operator on the phone. Nam's online order arrived damaged and in the wrong colour; Nam must explain the problem and choose between a refund and an exchange.
B is Yuki, whose family has a dog and who wants to adopt a cat. Nam must describe animals and how they behave, talk about nature in Thailand, and explain how things have changed over the years.
B is Yuki, who has started dating someone and asks Nam for advice. Nam must ask how things are going, share their own hopes and give gentle advice about a disagreement.

B is a staff member at the city disaster-prevention centre during a drill. Nam must ask what to do if an earthquake happens, check where the evacuation site is, and confirm what to keep ready at home.
B is Yamada-sensei in an end-of-year interview. Nam must explain what they wanted to be as a child, what they plan to do after the course, and what they can already do towards that goal.
B is a nurse at the university health check. Nam must describe their daily habits (sleep, meals, exercise), understand the nurse's advice and say what they will try to do or avoid from now on.
B is Yuki preparing a presentation on plastic waste in Thailand and Japan. Nam must explain causes and effects, say who is affected and how, and propose what individuals can do.
B is Yuki discussing the news over coffee. Nam must summarise a story they read (who did what to whom), report what people are saying about it and give their own view.

B is Yamada-sensei, who is curious about schools in Thailand. Nam must describe what teachers make students do, what students are and aren't allowed to do, and give an opinion on what schools should do.

B is a businessman staying at the hotel where Nam works part-time at the front desk. Nam must greet him, ask what he would like using honorific forms, explain the hotel services and give polite instructions.
B is a staff member of a client company calling Nam's office, where Nam is an intern. Nam must introduce themselves humbly, explain that the manager is out, take a message and arrange a visit.

B is an interviewer at a Japanese company's office in Bangkok. Nam must explain why they applied, talk about what they learned through part-time work and study, and say what role they could play in the company.
B is Yuki, who always runs out of money before payday. Nam must compare spending habits, complain about prices and suggest ways to save money and keep a budget.

B is an elderly neighbour who has just bought her first smartphone. Nam must explain step by step how to send a message and make a video call, warn her what not to do, and chat about how technology has changed life.
B is a Japanese businessman about to be posted to Bangkok. Nam must compare work culture, food, transport and climate in the two countries, and explain that not all Thai people are the same.

B is a Japanese exchange student who is going to Thailand next month. Nam must explain Thai manners (temples, monks, the head and feet), say what visitors should not do, and react to the Japanese customs the student describes.
B is Yuki at an izakaya after a long week. Nam must tell a funny or scary thing that happened to them, in order and with how they felt, and react to Yuki's own story.
B is Yuki, who is upset because Nam did not answer her messages for three days. Nam must explain what happened, clear up the misunderstanding and make up with her.

B is a Japanese tourist visiting Ayutthaya, where Nam is a volunteer guide. Nam must explain when and by whom the temples were built, what happened in history, and recommend a route and the best time to visit.

B is Yuki, who is writing a report on Thai food culture. Nam must explain how Thai people eat (sharing dishes, street food, eating little and often), compare this with Japanese habits and talk about their own eating habits.
B is a clerk at the ward office. Nam has just moved and must register their new address, ask which documents are needed, and understand what has to be done before what.

B is Yuki, who now works for a company and complains about overtime. Nam must ask about her working conditions, compare working styles in Thailand and Japan, and suggest realistic ways to balance work and life.
B is Yamada-sensei, whose mother now needs care. Nam must ask about his situation, explain how families care for older people in Thailand, and discuss what society should do.
B is Yuki, whose teenage cousin is being bullied online. Nam must discuss the risks of social media, give advice on privacy and online safety, and suggest what the family can do.

B is a staff member at the city's international centre interviewing Nam for its newsletter. Nam must describe the difficulties foreign residents face, what has helped them, and what Japanese society could do better.
B is Yuki, who doubts Nam's plan to open a small Thai café in Osaka with a friend. Nam must explain the idea, the budget and the risks, and answer Yuki's doubts with examples.

B is Yamada-sensei chairing a seminar where Nam presents survey results on how students use their smartphones. Nam must structure the talk, explain the data, define key terms and answer a question from the audience.

B is a Japanese classmate on the opposing side of a class debate about whether university should be free. Nam must state their position, acknowledge his good points and argue back politely with examples.

B is a Japanese high-school student who has to write a science report. Nam must explain a discovery, describe how the research was done and discuss both the benefits and the risks of a new technology.
B is Yuki after watching a film with Nam. Nam must summarise the story without spoiling the ending, give their impression of the acting and music, and recommend a Thai film or novel to her.

B is a Japanese journalist interviewing Nam about how young Thais see Japan. Nam must talk about Japanese companies and culture in Thailand, give examples from their own life and explain why the relationship matters.
B is the leader of a volunteer group at a local international festival. Nam must offer to help, ask what tasks there are and when, and explain why they want to volunteer.

B is Yuki at a shrine festival, where she buys an omikuji fortune with Nam. Nam must compare superstitions in Thailand and Japan, explain lucky and unlucky numbers and colours, and say how far they believe in them.

B is Yuki, who is thinking of moving to her grandparents' village and working remotely. Nam must compare city and country life, discuss the problems of shrinking villages and help her weigh up the pros and cons.

B is a Thai student who has just arrived in Japan and asks Nam for advice. Nam must talk about their own failures and what they learned from them, and give practical advice with examples from experience.

B is Nam's manager at a Japanese company in Bangkok, checking a draft email Nam wrote to a client. Nam must explain the purpose of the email, choose the right set phrases and fix expressions that are too casual.

B is Yamada-sensei helping Nam prepare a short farewell speech for their last day at the language school. Nam must thank people properly, look back on their time in Japan and express wishes for the future in formal Japanese.
